html:
The Union of Brest was a decision taken by Orthodox bishops of the Polish Lithuanian Commonwealth at a synod in Brest in October 1596 to accept the authority of the pope while keeping their Eastern rite.

The bishops sought protection from the Catholic king and equality with Catholic clergy. Many Orthodox clergy, nobles and Cossacks refused, and the Commonwealth's Ruthenian lands split into rival churches. The quarrel fed the Cossack wars of the 1600s. The new Greek Catholic church became the faith of most Belarusian peasants by the 1700s, until the Russian Empire abolished it in Belarus in 1839. In western Ukraine it survived and remains a national church.
sum: The Union of Brest was a decision taken by Orthodox bishops of the Polish Lithuanian Commonwealth at a synod in Brest in October 1596 to accept the authority of the pope while keeping their Eastern rite.
